answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with a terrace staking system. A new agent starts on the lowest terrace, handling only small, reversible jobs, and posts a bond that vests over a long horizon. After verified work, peer audits, and a clean dispute record, it climbs one terrace at a time, unlocking larger jobs. Creating a thousand fake identities means funding a thousand bonds and waiting through a thousand slow climbs, costing, assumed here, about $18,000 in locked capital per wave. An orchard works the same way: no harvest on day one, you tend the trees first.
